name: Songlin Zhao
intro: I study multimodal foundation models for medical images and text, and build research agents that connect models with usable workflows. My work spans volumetric segmentation, neuroimaging, and clinical research at Lehigh University and Mayo Clinic.

projects.name: OmniTumor
projects.summary: Text-prompted volumetric tumor and lesion segmentation across medical imaging modalities.
projects.role: First-author research on 3D vision-language modeling, data preparation, training and evaluation.
projects.details: This work brings natural-language prompts into volumetric segmentation. The research connects 3D CT, MRI and CBCT processing with multimodal alignment and clinically relevant evaluation.
projects.question: How can one model connect textual descriptions with tumors and lesions in three-dimensional images?

projects.name: BrainNet
projects.summary: A benchmark and toolkit for functional brain network construction and analysis.
projects.role: First-author research and development of benchmarking workflows for brain network analysis.
projects.details: BrainNet studies how connectivity construction affects downstream analysis. The toolkit supports systematic comparisons of brain-network methods, with common evaluation settings and reproducible pipelines.
projects.question: How much does the choice of connectivity construction change the conclusions of a brain network study?

projects.name: Multimodal normative modeling
projects.summary: Learning reference distributions to characterize individual deviations in brain imaging.
projects.role: Research on normative modeling, multimodal representation learning and individualized biomarkers.
projects.details: My work examines how multimodal neuroimaging can describe variation in brain development and disease. The central objective is a reliable reference distribution and meaningful individual deviation, with downstream clinical validation.
projects.question: How can multimodal reference models reveal meaningful individual differences in the brain?

projects.name: Research agents & tooling
projects.summary: Conversational tools for imaging workflows, retrieval and research evaluation.
projects.role: Agent application development, workflow integration and evaluation-oriented tooling.
projects.details: These projects explore how language models can call tools, retrieve relevant research context and help users navigate imaging pipelines. Public prototypes provide inspectable interfaces and implementation examples.
projects.question: How can research assistants connect natural-language requests to inspectable tools and outputs?
